from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 6  # sources
    J = 10  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [158, 177, 83, 139, 113, 200]
    demands = [49, 32, 42, 24, 19, 30, 15, 32, 54, 38]
    cost_matrix = [[9.21, 29.77, 24.64, 18.79, 10.68, 10.81, 14.28, 17.55, 3.32, 23.84], [28.1, 3.05, 9.62, 7.64, 4.82, 23.44, 9.7, 15.13, 18.54, 19.76], [8.64, 16.46, 23.1, 19.4, 9.83, 24.38, 12.44, 7.96, 20.6, 27.19], [17.09, 26.2, 4.83, 18.17, 14.29, 25.89, 20.64, 16.22, 14.63, 29.88], [15.4, 7.35, 13.56, 20.19, 12.96, 21.53, 27.36, 14.22, 7.29, 20.52], [15.3, 9.54, 29.68, 14.67, 19.65, 16.01, 24.75, 24.82, 25.93, 10.45]]
    emission_matrix = [[17.69, 12.4, 4.99, 8.45, 14.8, 9.12, 15.57, 12.95, 20.0, 6.88], [7.77, 6.77, 9.04, 10.17, 11.99, 10.04, 18.48, 12.44, 15.42, 2.93], [18.11, 5.45, 1.0, 8.62, 15.83, 12.25, 10.8, 18.69, 12.15, 4.95], [16.65, 8.55, 14.43, 11.51, 3.39, 15.03, 11.68, 1.96, 4.89, 8.37], [8.97, 11.32, 7.22, 5.68, 6.63, 4.76, 8.8, 2.78, 10.39, 3.61], [7.97, 17.07, 9.83, 8.6, 10.25, 16.15, 2.06, 9.89, 2.91, 11.06]]
    fixed_costs = [[266, 279, 222, 285, 142, 192, 155, 58, 278, 294], [133, 131, 163, 179, 227, 240, 194, 120, 188, 170], [150, 274, 139, 172, 199, 260, 61, 203, 240, 94], [88, 275, 264, 219, 172, 110, 174, 259, 284, 224], [262, 51, 61, 158, 226, 162, 227, 239, 96, 55], [154, 111, 82, 238, 106, 122, 193, 208, 92, 151]]
    moq = [[16, 16, 10, 15, 15, 20, 20, 13, 7, 18], [7, 6, 20, 14, 16, 8, 20, 11, 12, 6], [9, 5, 18, 17, 14, 20, 14, 20, 11, 17], [13, 5, 8, 9, 16, 7, 14, 8, 18, 19], [15, 11, 20, 19, 16, 17, 9, 11, 18, 16], [8, 18, 12, 10, 17, 18, 12, 20, 16, 11]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Supply Chain Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: Today
Subject: Balancing freight spend and carbon intensity in store replenishment

Context
Our replenishment network ships product from multiple warehouses to multiple stores. Each shipping lane has two performance signals: a monetary cost per unit and a carbon emission rate per unit. In practice, lanes with the lowest dollar cost often carry a higher carbon footprint. We must deliver reliable service at competitive cost while continuing to reduce emissions in line with our sustainability commitments. Balancing these aims requires a clear, data-driven shipping plan that respects real-world operating rules on contracting and execution.

Operational rules to reflect day-to-day realities
- Route activation costs: Any lane we use requires a fixed activation fee to cover contracting, compliance, and dock readiness. A lane is either active or not; once active, the fee applies regardless of the volume we ship.
- Minimum order quantities per active lane: To avoid partial loads and inefficient handling, any lane we activate must move at least its specified minimum. If we cannot meet that minimum, we should not activate the lane.
- Supplier limits per store: To reduce receiving congestion, vendor management overhead, and invoice complexity, each store may be served by no more than the permitted maximum number of warehouses.

Supply and demand guardrails
- Each warehouse has finite inventory and throughput capacity. Our plan cannot allocate more than what is available at any warehouse.
- Each store has a minimum demand that must be fulfilled to protect in-stock rates. Our plan must meet at least that level at every location.

Management priority
Leadership has set relative importance weights that favor cost while still placing meaningful emphasis on emissions. We will evaluate candidate plans using a blended view: variable shipping costs will be weighted by the cost importance, total emissions will be weighted by the emissions importance, and route activation fees will be added at full value. This approach ensures we reflect the true economics of opening lanes while advancing our sustainability agenda.

Business goal
Identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each so that:
- All store demand floors are met without exceeding warehouse inventory,
- Any activated lane ships at least its minimum volume,
- Each store is served by no more than the allowed number of warehouses,
- The overall blended total—combining weighted variable cost, weighted emissions, and full activation fees—is as low as possible.

What this delivers
- A clear list of lanes to activate and lanes to keep inactive,
- Shipment quantities by active lane that satisfy demand and respect supply,
- Store-to-warehouse assignments that observe the supplier cap,
- A transparent scorecard showing total variable cost, total emissions, and total activation fees under the agreed importance weights.
